class.name: FellowTerrain3D
class.brief_description: A height field terrain with continuous levels of detail, blended materials, collision and height queries (FellowEngine).
class.description: A terrain made from [member heightmap], an [Image] of heights in metres ([constant Image.FORMAT_RF]), one texel per vertex, [member vertex_spacing] metres apart: a 1025 × 1025 image at 1 m is a 1 km square. Its local origin is the heightmap's first texel; x runs along the image's width, z along its height. It is drawn with continuous distance-dependent levels of detail (CDLOD): a quadtree of square patches of [member patch_size] × [member patch_size] quads, each level's cells twice the size of the finer one's, chosen around the camera every frame it moves. Before a coarser level takes over, a patch's vertices morph onto the coarser grid, and its heights are read from a coarser mipmap of the heightmap as they do, so neighbouring levels meet without cracks and change without popping. All patches are instances of one [MultiMesh] (one draw per pass); FellowEngine's MultiMesh culling ([member ProjectSettings.rendering/fellow/geometry/multimesh_culling]) culls them one by one in the camera's and the shadows' passes. When the selection changes, the new patches are written into a second, hidden MultiMesh and shown three drawn frames later, so the motion vectors (TAA, FSR) of the ground are always those of a static surface. Up to 9 [member layers] are blended: layer 0 is the base, [member splat_map]'s red, green, blue and alpha channels the weights of layers 1 to 4 and [member splat_map_2]'s those of layers 5 to 8 (the base takes what they leave). With [member height_blend], a layer with a height in its albedo's alpha shows through where it is higher. FellowEngine's weather (wetness, puddles, snow cover, [FellowRain3D]) applies to the terrain as to any material. With [member collision_enabled], the terrain is a static physics body of height map shapes, one per region of [member collision_region_size] cells, the same triangles as its finest level of detail. [method get_height], [method get_normal] and [method get_layer_weights] answer from the CPU's copy of the data. [member hole_map] cuts holes (a cave's mouth, a tunnel's portal): a triangle touching a marked vertex is neither drawn nor collides, and no foliage grows on it. The patches over holes are drawn with a second material that discards those triangles; the rest of the terrain keeps the material without a discard. [method paint_holes] cuts and fills them with a brush. [method sculpt] and [method paint] change the heights and the layers' weights around a point and update only that region (the editor's toolbar for a selected terrain sculpts and paints with them, with undo). After changing the [member heightmap] image's pixels in place yourself, call [method update_heightmap]. A large heightmap is best saved as its own resource ([code].res[/code]) rather than inside the scene. In the editor, the levels of detail follow the 3D editor's camera.

method.name: blit_heightmap_region
method.description: Writes [param region] (heights in metres, [constant Image.FORMAT_RF]; other formats as [method heightmap_from_image] maps them from 0..1 to 0..1 m) into [member heightmap] with its first texel at [param position], and updates only what it covers: as [method sculpt] does. Used by the editor's undo; a game can stamp a crater or a building's pad with it.

method.name: blit_splat_region
method.description: Writes [param region] (weights, converted to [constant Image.FORMAT_RGBA8]) into [member splat_map] ([param map] 0) or [member splat_map_2] ([param map] 1) with its first texel at [param position], and updates only what it covers: as [method paint] does. The splat map must already be an RGBA8 image without mipmaps (as [method paint] leaves it).

method.name: bake_foliage_impostors
method.description: Bakes the impostor of every [member foliage] kind with a mesh and a [member FellowTerrainFoliage.impostor_distance]: its mesh rendered from [param frames] × [param frames] directions over the sphere (octahedral views of [param resolution] pixels, the albedo with coverage and the normal), one view a frame in this terrain's world, saved in [param directory] as [code]<terrain>_foliage_<index>_<mesh>_impostor.res[/code] (a quad mesh with its material and its atlases, lossless), and set as the kind's [member FellowTerrainFoliage.impostor]. Returns the number of kinds queued; [signal foliage_impostors_baked] is emitted when they are all saved. The terrain must be in the tree, with the Forward+ or Mobile renderer (the editor's Bake Impostors button for a selected terrain saves them next to the scene, in [code]impostors/[/code], with undo).

method.name: blit_hole_region
method.description: Writes [param region] (converted to [constant Image.FORMAT_L8]: above half a hole) into [member hole_map] with its first texel at [param position], and updates only what it covers: as [method paint_holes] does. Used by the editor's undo.

method.name: get_aabb
method.description: The terrain's box in its local space: from its origin to the far corner of the heightmap, from the lowest height to the highest.

method.name: get_height
method.description: The ground's height (global y) under [param global_position], on the triangles of the finest level of detail (and of the collision shapes). NaN outside the heightmap.

method.name: get_layer_weights
method.description: The 9 layers' weights at [param global_position], from the splat maps (nearest texel, before the height blend): layer 0's is what the others leave of 1.

method.name: get_material
method.description: The [ShaderMaterial] the terrain draws with (shared code; its parameters are set from the node's properties and layers). Read only: changes are overwritten.

method.name: get_normal
method.description: The ground's normal (global) at [param global_position], from central differences of the heights one [member vertex_spacing] apart. A zero vector outside the heightmap.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: The current selection and data: [code]patches[/code], [code]triangles[/code], [code]patches_per_level[/code], [code]levels[/code], [code skip-lint]lod_distance[/code] (the finest level's range in metres), [code]selections[/code] and [code]swaps[/code] (the selections computed and the MultiMesh switches since the start), [code]last_select_usec[/code], [code]collision_shapes[/code], [code]edit_flush_usec[/code] (the last update of the textures and collision shapes after edits, at a frame's end), [code]map_size[/code], [code]process_usec_mean[/code], [code]process_usec_max[/code] and [code]process_usec_last[/code] (the main thread's time in the terrain's frames: its levels of detail and foliage), [code]foliage_cells[/code] and [code]foliage_instances[/code] (the foliage's cells made and the instances drawn in them).

method.name: is_hole
method.description: Whether the terrain has a hole under [param global_position] (in a triangle that touches a vertex of [member hole_map]). [method get_height] returns NaN there.

method.name: heightmap_from_image
method.description: A heightmap for [member heightmap] from [param image]: a grey image ([constant Image.FORMAT_L8], 16-bit, any colour format: its red channel) mapped from 0..1 to [param min_height]..[param max_height] metres, or a [constant Image.FORMAT_RF] or [constant Image.FORMAT_RH] image of metres kept as it is. Mipmaps are dropped; compressed images are decompressed.

method.name: paint
method.description: Paints [param layer] (0-8) into the splat maps around [param global_position], [param radius] metres around it, with a smooth falloff: every layer's weight moves towards 0 and [param layer]'s towards 1 by [param strength] (0..1) at the centre, so that the weights still add up to 1. When there is no [member splat_map] yet, one is made (RGBA8, the heightmap's size); [member splat_map_2] is made when a layer above 4 is painted. A splat map in another format, or with mipmaps, is converted to RGBA8 without them first. Only the splat maps' texels within the brush are updated: their textures, the CPU's copy the queries and the foliage read, and the foliage cells over them (scattered again).

method.name: paint_holes
method.description: Marks ([param hole] [code]true[/code]) or clears the vertices within [param radius] metres of [param global_position] in [member hole_map] (made, L8 at the heightmap's size, when there is none). The triangles touching a marked vertex are no longer drawn, collide no more (their heights are NaN in the collision shapes: Godot's 3D physics, Jolt, has no collision in such a triangle) and lose their foliage. Only the region is updated: the hole texture, the patches over holes, the foliage cells and the collision shapes over it.

method.name: sculpt
method.description: Changes the heights around [param global_position], [param radius] metres around it, with a smooth falloff ([code](1 - d²)²[/code] of the distance as a share of the radius): [constant SCULPT_RAISE] and [constant SCULPT_LOWER] by [param strength] metres at the centre, [constant SCULPT_SMOOTH] towards the mean of each texel's neighbours and [constant SCULPT_FLATTEN] towards [param target_height], both by [param strength] (0..1) of the way at the centre. A heightmap in another format than [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], or with mipmaps, is replaced by an RF image of the heights first. Only what the brush touched is updated: at once the heights' CPU copy (the queries answer from it), the levels' bounds, the normals and the mipmaps over the region (as [method Image.generate_mipmaps] makes them), and the foliage cells over it (scattered again); at the frame's end, once for all the frame's edits, the height and normal textures (uploaded again whole) and the collision shapes over the edited region. The result is the terrain a rebuild from the edited [member heightmap] makes, texel for texel. Usable in a game (craters, paths); in the editor, the terrain's toolbar in the 3D view sculpts and paints with undo.

method.name: update_heightmap
method.description: Builds the terrain's data again from [member heightmap], [member splat_map] and [member splat_map_2]: the textures, the normals, the levels' bounds, the collision shapes. Call it after editing an image in place.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the terrain casts shadows.
If [code]true[/code], the terrain is a static physics body (height map shapes, one per [member collision_region_size] region).
The physics layers the terrain is in.
The physics layers the terrain scans.
The cells along a collision shape's side: the heightmap is cut into regions of this size, each its own height map shape.
Draws the terrain in a diagnostic view instead of its layers.
The kinds of plants and rocks the terrain scatters over its layers around the camera ([FellowTerrainFoliage]).
At most this many foliage cells are started a frame (each made on a worker thread): fewer spread a fast camera's new cells over more frames.

How much the layers' heights (their albedo's alpha, with [member FellowTerrainLayer.height_in_albedo_alpha]) decide where they show: 0 blends by the weights alone; higher values give sharper transitions where the higher layer wins.

Holes in the terrain (decision 0172): an image of the heightmap's size (another size is stretched over it, nearest texel), a texel above half a hole at that vertex. A triangle touching a hole's vertex is not drawn (the patches over holes use a second material that discards it), does not collide and has no foliage; [method get_height] returns NaN over it and [method is_hole] [code]true[/code]. Without a hole map (the default) the terrain draws as before, with its material only.
The heights in metres, one texel per vertex ([constant Image.FORMAT_RF]; another format is converted as [method heightmap_from_image] does with 0..1 metres). At least 2 × 2 texels.
The terrain's materials, at most 9: layer 0 is the base, layers 1 to 8 are weighted by [member splat_map] and [member splat_map_2].
The range of the finest level of detail in metres (each coarser level's twice the one before). 0: three times the finest level's node (two patches). At least two and a half times it.
A large-scale variation of the albedo's brightness (two octaves of noise, 75 m and 14 m), against visible tiling at a distance.
Where between a level's range and the finer level's its vertices begin to morph onto the coarser grid (0.7: in the last 30 % of the way).
The quads along a patch's side (8, 16, 32 or 64): smaller patches follow the distance more closely, larger ones make fewer instances.
The render layers the terrain is drawn in ([member VisualInstance3D.layers]).
The weights of layers 1 to 4 in its red, green, blue and alpha channels, stretched over the whole terrain (any resolution).
The weights of layers 5 to 8 in its red, green, blue and alpha channels.
The distance between two vertices (two heightmap texels) in metres.

signal.name: foliage_impostors_baked
signal.description: Emitted when [method bake_foliage_impostors] has saved every impostor it queued, with their files.

constants.constant: Raises the ground by the strength in metres at the brush's centre.
Lowers the ground by the strength in metres at the brush's centre.
Moves each height towards the mean of its 3 × 3 neighbourhood, by the strength (0..1) of the way at the centre.
Moves each height towards the target height, by the strength (0..1) of the way at the centre.
The ground coloured by its level of detail (red the finest, then yellow, green, blue, purple, grey), blended towards the next colour as it morphs to the next level.
